epic.title: compat(diagnostics): process-gone events, crashReporter local-state facade, app metrics census and Bun-side process stats (contentTracing never)
epic.body:
## Scope
12 entities / 63 members: crashReporter (8), contentTracing (5), app metrics/GPU structures, process memory/CPU methods. Corpus demand for the module surfaces is zero; adjacent demand is real: draw.io listens to `render-process-gone` and installs `uncaughtException → app.exit(1)` in export mode; Zettlr handles `unresponsive` → destroy and logs `unhandledRejection`; both call `disableHardwareAcceleration()` before ready.

## Maturity ladder
- L0: every member exists; contentTracing rejects with the arch 07 structured compat error; never rows published.
- L1: `render-process-gone` from engine web-content-process termination (WKWebView webContentProcessDidTerminate; WebView2 ProcessFailed beside the existing BrowserProcessExited observation; WebKitGTK web-process-terminated); Bun-side `process.getHeapStatistics/getCPUUsage/getProcessMemoryInfo` with documented ▲ fields.
- L2: `getAppMetrics` as the arch 01 §5.1 census (host = Browser row; guardian; Bun primary = Utility `keld.primary`; named roles) with KiB units; crashReporter local-state facade at BEHAVIOR_MATCH.

## Linear owners consumed
KEL-105/KEL-116 (crash ledger), KEL-90/KEL-129 (census rules), KEL-75 (generations), KEL-143, KEL-78, KEL-132 (GpuSafeMode).

## Design facts fixed by research (two refuters)
- Bun-primary death is never mapped to any Electron event; a host-emitted process-gone family over the app link feeds `render-process-gone` and `child-process-gone` facades with reason fidelity recorded per engine.
- crashReporter is a local-state facade (start/add/remove/get/setUploadToServer; getLastCrashReport null; getUploadedReports []); keys ≥ 40 bytes ignored with a warning, values truncated (documented); no uploader, no minidumps.
- `getAppMetrics` consumes the §5.1 census (KiB, `>> 10`); percentCPUUsage normalised by CPU count with a per-process last sample.
- contentTracing: never, with Promise rejections for the Promise-returning methods; GPU getters are a research atom (Linux GpuSafeMode yields at most one derived fact).

refuter_verdicts_batch1.lens: Keld invariants, ownership and reuse (four uniques; default-deny never defaulted to allow; no Electron-isms in keld-core/keld-ipc; no parallel process model/transport/schema/parser/policy owner; reuse of KEL-75/76/77/78/79/80/53/74/102/135/139-144 owners; measured performance; spec+Linear gate; #312/#313/#319/#322/#323/#325 and KEL-127). Verified against origin/main d150a14 sources, pinned Electron v44.4.5 docs and Electron source copies in scratchpad/f08-refute, a live Bun 1.4.2+744846f84 probe, and the corpus clones.

verdicts.reason: Every load-bearing fact checks out: no minidump/crashpad/upload code anywhere in crates/; keld-guard evaluates `net.connect` with URL scopes (crates/keld-guard/src/lib.rs tests at 1601-1695) so an upload would have exactly one gate; CrashLedger/SelfTerminationRecord exist as described (crates/keld-runtime/src/lib.rs:527-580); Electron's cr.ts derives getLastCrashReport from getUploadedReports (uploaded-only, f08-refute/cr.ts:51-62); the corpus has zero crashReporter call sites (grep over drawio-desktop/src, zettlr/source, electron-quick-start). The local-state facade with no network path keeps default-deny intact, reuses the one crash-fact owner, and the ▲ is explicit per KEL-127. The user-owned 'ever upload?' blocker is genuine.
verdicts.evidence: crates/keld-guard/src/lib.rs (net.connect scope tests 1601-1695; `audit` top-level key ignored at 565); crates/keld-runtime/src/lib.rs:527-580; f08-refute/cr.ts:14-62 (start() throws only when uploadToServer && !submitURL; no already-started guard in JS; globalExtra amended with _productName/_version/_companyName via app.getVersion()); f08-refute/crash_keys.cc:48-62 (key.size() >= 40 → EmitWarning + ignore, never throw); api_crash-reporter.md:100-140,204-226.
verdicts.correction: Three of the stated unknowns are now settled from source and must be written into the cell: (1) getParameters()/other methods before start() do not throw in JS (cr.ts calls the binding directly) — the Electron oracle for 'other-method-before-start' is 'no throw'; (2) an over-long key (>=40 bytes) is warned and silently ignored, not rejected or thrown; values are bounded by CrashKeyString<20320> (truncation is an inference from Chromium CrashKeyString semantics, not shown in the copied source — still needs the oracle run); (3) BEHAVIOR_MATCH for getParameters() requires the facade to inject `_productName`, `_version` (and `_companyName` when given) exactly as cr.ts does, which depends on app.getVersion()/app.getName() — neither exists in @keld/electron today (packages/@keld/electron/src/app.ts), so D1 has an unlisted dependency on the app facade (F01/F02 territory).

verdicts.reason: Two factual claims are wrong and one fidelity assumption has no Keld owner. (a) 'keld-wv WebView2 backend registers only NavigationCompleted' is false: crates/keld-wv/src/webview2/mod.rs registers add_BrowserProcessExited (line 1259, environment-level, reads BrowserProcessId + BrowserProcessExitKind against an expected pid for profile-release lifecycle), add_PermissionRequested (1927), add_NewWindowRequested (1946) and add_NavigationCompleted (1995). An engine-process-exit observation already exists and must be the reuse point, not 'no owner today'. (b) Mapping named-role clean exits onto app 'child-process-gone' with reason clean-exit contradicts Electron's emission path: f08-refute/app.cc:814-848 emits child-process-gone only from BrowserChildProcessCrashed/BrowserChildProcessKilled; BrowserChildProcessHostDisconnected (normal exit) only drops the metrics row. The pinned doc lists clean-exit as a vocabulary value, but the source gives no emission for a zero exit; the semantic-trap oracle 'two events, clean-exit (exitCode 0) and killed' is therefore unverified and probably wrong. (c) Reason fidelity for roles is asserted as 'clean-exit/abnormal-exit/killed by exit status/signal', but Keld's role exit observation carries no status at all (RoleEvent::Revoked { generation, attempt, cause: RoleRevocationCause::ChildExited } at crates/keld-runtime/src/role.rs:317-324, 248-264) and the per-role ledger (RoleSupervisor::crash_ledger(), role.rs:629) records only SelfTerminationRecord.exit_code: Option<i32> with None for any signal — no signal number. 'killed' (SIGTERM/SIGKILL) and 'crashed' (SIGSEGV/SIGABRT) are indistinguishable from Keld's own owner today.
verdicts.evidence: crates/keld-wv/src/webview2/mod.rs:1229-1263 (BrowserProcessExitedEventHandler, expected_pid, matching_browser_exit), 1927, 1946, 1995; f08-refute/app.cc:806-848; f08-refute/api_app.md:415-440; crates/keld-runtime/src/role.rs:248-264, 286-324, 629; crates/keld-runtime/src/lib.rs:161-195 (ChildCrashed { pid, exit_code, stderr_tail } — no signal), 499-506 (SupervisorEvent::Exited { pid, code }), 516-518 (Stopped: exit zero stops supervision, no restart); docs/architecture/06-runtime-and-tooling.md:346-349 ('Status zero does not consume crash-loop budget or restart').
verdicts.correction: Rewrite D2 as: (1) WebView2: extend the existing BrowserProcessExited observation (environment level, browser-process pid already known) and add add_ProcessFailed beside it in the same module — name keld-wv/KEL-132-adjacent as the owner, not 'no owner'. (2) Named-role clean exit maps to the utilityProcess facade's own 'exit' event (KEL-75 facade; fetch utility-process.md v44.4.5 as the receipt — not in current receipts), and app 'child-process-gone' is emitted only for crash/kill-class role terminations; replace the trap oracle with: exit-0 role → Electron oracle run must confirm no child-process-gone; SIGKILL role → exactly one event. (3) Add a blocker on the supervisor owner (KEL-116 fixed-size SelfTerminationRecord): record the terminating signal (std::os::unix::process::ExitStatusExt::signal(), allocation-free Option<i32>) so 'killed' vs 'crashed' vs 'oom' is a fact, not a guess; until then any reason other than abnormal-exit/clean-exit for a signal death is fabricated. (4) State that the Bun-primary 'successor reads predecessor' KEL-143 contract applies to crash-class exits only — a status-zero primary exit ends supervision (SupervisorEvent::Stopped), which matches Electron's main exiting.

verdicts.reason: The one-owner census argument holds against the sources: arch 01 §5.1 (docs/architecture/01-overview.md:196-226) and decisions §15 (docs/engineering/decisions.md:893-899) fix the keld-owned census (host, guardian re-exec, Bun primary, named roles) with engine helpers 'reported as separate diagnostics'; no census code exists in crates (grep hits only keld-runtime tests/guardian); WebView2 GetProcessInfos and ProcessFailed receipts verified in f08-refute/ms-env8.html and ms-pfe2.html. Electron's own ProcessMetric derivation (f08-refute/app.cc:1470-1505) matches the proposed field set (creationTime, serviceName=metrics_name, sandboxed, integrityLevel). Appending engine rows only where a public API enumerates them keeps §5.1's exclusion explicit rather than inventing a parallel ppid census.
verdicts.evidence: docs/architecture/01-overview.md:216,222; docs/engineering/decisions.md:893-899; f08-refute/app.cc:1485-1493 (workingSetSize/peakWorkingSetSize/privateBytes = bytes >> 10), 1500-1505; f08-refute/process_metric.cc:84-86,155-156; crates/keld-wv/src/webview2/mod.rs:1229-1263 (host already tracks the WebView2 browser pid); docs/architecture/04-electron-compat.md:117-125 ('PID is diagnostic only, never a Keld identity or control handle'); docs/agents/learnings.md:158.
verdicts.correction: (1) Delete the 'Kilobytes divisor 1000 vs 1024' unknown: app.cc:1485-1493 uses `>> 10`, i.e. KiB, which is also §5.1's unit — no oracle run needed. (2) Name the contract owner: getAppMetrics is a new host CALL, so it must be minted through the existing echo-codegen contract source (KEL-98; KEL-127 'one minimal contract source, no new IDL'), not an ad hoc kipc message. (3) On Windows the host already knows the WebView2 browser-process pid from the BrowserProcessExited observation; the engine-row source is GetProcessInfos plus that pid, and the learnings 2026-08-24 [bench/windows] churn rule means engine rows must be labeled timing-dependent. (4) integrityLevel for the LPAC primary stays unknown (docs/specs/kel210-windows-lpac-primary.md names no integrity level) — cheapest check: read the token integrity RID of a live LPAC primary with GetTokenInformation(TokenIntegrityLevel) in the KEL-210 fixture.

verdicts.reason: Re-ran the probe on Bun 1.4.2+744846f84: process.memoryUsage(), process.cpuUsage(), process.resourceUsage(), node:v8.getHeapStatistics() (all 14 snake_case fields) and process.abort are present; process.type is undefined natively. Electron's bindings confirm the shapes the facade must mirror: heap statistics are bytes >> 10 (KiB), getProcessMemoryInfo sets residentSet only under IS_LINUX || IS_WIN, and process.crash()/hang() are plain main-thread crash/hang. Serving self-process metrics from Bun with no host round trip respects reuse-before-rewrite and keeps kipc hot paths untouched.
verdicts.evidence: scratchpad/f08-bun-probe.ts run 2026-10-06 (bun --revision 1.4.2+744846f84); f08-refute/bindings.cc:128-150 (>> 10), 255-270 (#if IS_LINUX||IS_WIN residentSet; promise rejects 'Failed to create memory dump' / 'Failed to find current process memory details'), 274-300 (percentCPUUsage = usagePercent / NumberOfProcessors; idleWakeupsPerSecond 0 on Windows); f08-refute/api_process.md:150-206; crates/keld-runtime/src/lib.rs:527-540 (SelfTerminationRecord.exit_code None for signal).
verdicts.correction: (1) Divisor settled: KiB (>> 10) for getHeapStatistics and getAppMetrics; drop the unknown. (2) Add a missed semantic trap: Electron divides percentCPUUsage by the processor count (bindings.cc:290), so a facade computing process.cpuUsage() deltas / wall time must also divide by os.cpus().length or it over-reports by up to N×. (3) getProcessMemoryInfo in Electron can reject; the facade's Promise must keep a rejection path for the fields it cannot derive rather than resolving with undefined. (4) The probe shows Bun's v8 shim is numerically degenerate (total_heap_size == used_heap_size == malloced_memory == 140250; total_physical_size == peak_malloced_memory == 14417920), so the ▲ must say values are JSC-derived and not comparable to Electron's, not merely 'renamed'. (5) crash() → process.abort() yields exit_code None, which the ledger cannot distinguish from SIGKILL (see D2 correction); the trap oracle 'SIGABRT appears as exit_code None' is true but weak until a signal field exists.

verdicts.reason: The decision is right on the invariants: arch 07 §2 requires structured compat errors (docs/architecture/07-agent-experience.md:54-60), the briefing never-list #10 forbids production CDP/Chromium flags, KEL-127 forbids a silent no-op, and the corpus has zero contentTracing call sites. Pinned content-tracing.md (f08-refute/api_content-tracing.md:11,74-75,103) matches the quoted semantics. WebKit has no Chromium tracing service, so there is no honest analog.
verdicts.evidence: docs/architecture/07-agent-experience.md:49-60; crates/keld-cli/tests/error_registry.rs:22-38 (scan roots are crates/* and keld-cli/templates only; packages/ is not scanned); docs/engineering/keld-error-codes.md:593-647 (KELD-COMPAT-001..009 are all keld-compat evidence-schema codes); packages/@keld/kipc/src/transport.ts:1043-1050 (KeldCallError = Error & { code: string } — no tier/issue/workaround fields); packages/@keld/electron/src/link.ts (re-export only).
verdicts.correction: The proof mechanism named in the trap ('registry test proves the code is documented') does not hold today for a TypeScript-side throw: error_registry.rs scans only Rust crates and keld-cli templates, every existing KELD-COMPAT-* code belongs to the evidence schema in crates/keld-compat, and @keld/electron has no structured compat error type (KeldCallError carries only `code`). Before any contentTracing cell lands: extend error_registry.rs scan roots to packages/@keld/*/src (or mint the codes from Rust), reserve a code range distinct from KELD-COMPAT-001..009, and give @keld/electron one error shape with code, tier status, tracking issue and workaround as arch 07 §2 requires — this is a prerequisite shared by every 'documented-never' cell in the program, not F08-specific.

verdicts.reason: The proposed answer says KEL-132's GpuSafeMode 'can honestly drive gpu_compositing and rasterization as enabled vs disabled_software/disabled_off_ok'. The code says otherwise: GpuSafeMode is an NVIDIA+Wayland DMA-BUF mitigation state, not a GPU-feature probe. `Normal` is documented as 'No known-risky driver/session combination detected' (crates/keld-wv/src/webkitgtk/mod.rs:62-72) and detect_gpu_safe_mode_with returns Normal for every non-NVIDIA or non-Wayland session regardless of whether WebKitGTK is hardware-accelerated. Emitting 'enabled' from Normal would be the fabrication the atom itself forbids, and even NvidiaWaylandDmabufDisabled only proves the DMA-BUF renderer is off, not that compositing or rasterization is software. The Linux-has-a-signal premise is therefore overstated; today no Keld owner can prove any GPUFeatureStatus field on any OS.
verdicts.evidence: crates/keld-wv/src/webkitgtk/mod.rs:55-135 (enum docs, is_degraded, reason strings, detect_gpu_safe_mode_with); docs/specs/kel132-webview-gpu-media.md:49-53,112,261-262; docs/architecture/05-webview-and-native.md:93-103; f08-refute/app.cc:1155-1160 (DisableHardwareAcceleration after ready → ThrowError 'can only be called before app is ready'), 1514-1535 (GetGPUFeatureStatus is a synchronous content::GetFeatureStatus(); GetGPUInfo rejects 'Invalid info type' / 'GPU access not allowed'); f08-refute/api_structures_gpu-feature-status.md (no 'unknown' value); corpus: drawio-desktop/src/main/electron.js:166 and zettlr/source/main.ts:79 call disableHardwareAcceleration().
verdicts.correction: (1) Replace the Linux mapping claim with: GpuSafeMode supports at most one derived fact — when is_degraded() is true, the DMA-BUF renderer is disabled — which maps to no GPUFeatureStatus field without a KEL-132-owned ruling; getGPUFeatureStatus returns an empty partial structure under the ▲ flag until a real engine signal exists. (2) Two unknowns are settled from Electron source: disableHardwareAcceleration() after ready throws with the exact message above (the Keld facade must throw identically), and getGPUFeatureStatus has no readiness throw in source (the doc's 'only usable after gpu-info-update' is advisory). (3) The cheapest experiments that would move this from research to a decision: read ICoreWebView2EnvironmentOptions.AdditionalBrowserArguments for a Microsoft receipt on --disable-gpu under a shared user-data folder (WebView2), and confirm WebKitGTK's webkit_settings_set_hardware_acceleration_policy as the single named Linux policy for disableHardwareAcceleration — both are host-owned single policies, not 'arbitrary flags', but need KEL-132 spec amendment and remain unverified here.

extra_findings.finding: Supervisor records no terminating signal. RuntimeError::ChildCrashed carries { pid, exit_code: Option<i32>, stderr_tail } and SelfTerminationRecord carries exit_code: Option<i32> only; every signal death collapses to None. Any Electron reason finer than abnormal-exit (killed / crashed / oom) for a Bun generation or named role is unprovable until KEL-116's fixed-size record gains an allocation-free signal field. This blocks D2's reason fidelity and weakens the D4 crash() oracle.

Electron emits app 'child-process-gone' only from the crashed/killed observer callbacks; a normal child exit only disconnects the metrics row. The research object's child-process-gone trap oracle (exit-0 role → clean-exit event) is contradicted by source and must be re-run against a real Electron oracle; clean exits belong to the utilityProcess 'exit' event (receipt not yet collected: utility-process.md v44.4.5).

The error-code registry gate does not cover TypeScript. crates/keld-cli/tests/error_registry.rs scans only crates/*/src and keld-cli/templates; all nine existing KELD-COMPAT-* codes are keld-compat evidence-schema codes; @keld/electron's only error type is KeldCallError = Error & { code }. The 'structured compat error + registry test' proof cited by D5 and by every documented-never cell has no owner yet — it is a program-wide prerequisite, not an F08 detail.

Electron normalizes percentCPUUsage by NumberOfProcessors (bindings.cc:290). A Bun-side getCPUUsage facade that computes cpuUsage deltas over wall time without dividing by core count over-reports by up to N×; the object's CPUUsage trap omits this.

Oracle pin drift: the committed lifecycle corpus pins oracle ids at electron-v44.3.0 while this map pins v44.4.5 and the briefing notes v44.5.1 is current. KEL-74 denominator honesty requires one declared oracle per cell; any F08 cell landing in the same panel needs a ruling on per-cell versus per-panel oracle version before it can be scored.

WebView2 engine-process lifecycle is already partially wired: keld-wv registers add_BrowserProcessExited with an expected browser pid for profile release. D2's 'keld-wv wires no engine process-failure hook (no owner today)' understates the live code; the correct plan is to extend this owner (same module, same handler pattern) with add_ProcessFailed and to reuse the known browser pid for D3's Windows engine rows.

crashReporter.start() in Electron calls app.getVersion() and injects _productName/_version/_companyName into the global crash keys; getParameters() BEHAVIOR_MATCH therefore depends on app.getVersion()/app.getName(), which @keld/electron does not implement. D1 has an undeclared cross-unit dependency on the app facade.

Electron behavior now settled from source for three stated unknowns: getParameters()/other methods before start() do not throw in JS; a crash-key name of 40+ bytes is warned and ignored (never thrown); disableHardwareAcceleration() after ready throws 'app.disableHardwareAcceleration() can only be called before app is ready'. The object should cite these rather than schedule oracle runs for them.

A status-zero Bun primary exit stops supervision without restart (SupervisorEvent::Stopped; arch 06 'Status zero does not consume crash-loop budget or restart'), and the live KELD-RUNTIME-012 text tells the app to stay alive while the host-owned session is active. The KEL-143 'successor reads predecessor' contract therefore applies to crash-class exits only; D2 should say so explicitly so process.exit(0) in main is not mistaken for a recoverable event.

The manifest `audit` top-level key is ignored by the live parser (guard lib.rs doc: 'Unknown top-level keys ($schema, windows, audit) are ignored'), so the reuse point 'arch 03 §2 audit.log as the future owner of local crash records' has no parser or sink today; naming it is fine, but any crash-record persistence proposal must route through KEL-102 schema work first, not assume the key is live.

So the sequencing answer is: (1) land the host-emitted engine process-gone and Bun-generation-gone events first (they ride on live keld-runtime CrashLedger/KEL-75 generations and on engine hooks keld-wv has not yet wired: WKWebView webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate, WebView2 ProcessFailed, WebKitGTK web-process-terminated); (2) ship process.getHeapStatistics/getCPUUsage/getProcessMemoryInfo as a pure Bun-side facade (Bun 1.4.2 exposes process.memoryUsage, process.cpuUsage, process.resourceUsage, node:v8.getHeapStatistics, bun:jsc heapStats — probed live) with KB conversion and documented ▲ for fields Bun cannot derive (private/shared); (3) ship crashReporter as a local-state facade (start/addExtraParameter/removeExtraParameter/getParameters/get/setUploadToServer BEHAVIOR_MATCH-capable because they are pure data; getLastCrashReport/getUploadedReports honestly return null/[] because Keld has no uploader, and Electron itself only returns UPLOADED reports) with upload gated behind an explicit `net.connect` grant + opt-in — Electron's default uploadToServer:true cannot survive default-deny and is a documented ▲; (4) app.getAppMetrics must consume architecture 01 §5.1's ruled census (keld-owned processes: host, macOS guardian, Bun primary, named roles; engine helpers are separate diagnostics) and its counters (resident set + private companion, KiB) rather than inventing a second census; WebView2 GetProcessInfos gives pid+kind only (caller reads memory itself), WKWebView exposes no public web-process pid; (5) contentTracing is a documented-never in production (Chromium tracing service; WebKit has none; briefing never-list #10) delivered as an arch 07 §2 structured error; (6) GPUFeatureStatus/getGPUInfo are research: only Linux has a Keld-owned signal today (KEL-132 GpuSafeMode three-state), the enum has no 'unknown' value, so an honest mapping needs a ruling. Live Keld today: keld_runtime::CrashLedger {count, last (KELD-RUNTIME-012 + bounded stderr tail 64 KiB head / 192 KiB tail), stdout_len_at_last_crash, self_termination_count, last_self_termination}, Supervisor::crash_ledger()/current_pid(), KELD-RUNTIME-002 breaker (3 crashes/30 s sliding), KELD-CORE-033 surfacing in the no-flag host; @keld/electron exports only `app`; no crash dumps, no uploader, no process census code, no engine process-failure hooks, no GPU status API. Key new observable with no Electron analog: in Keld the developer "main" (Bun) can crash and be replaced while the host-owned window survives; the restarted generation could be told about its predecessor's death — that needs a Keld-named contract (KEL-143 territory), not an Electron API name.

decisions.question: What does the Tier-2 'crashReporter map' honestly mean in Keld, given Keld has no crash-dump capture or uploader and default-deny forbids Electron's uploadToServer:true default?
decisions.proposed_answer: crashReporter becomes a local-state facade in @keld/electron: start(options) validates and stores {submitURL, productName (default app name), uploadToServer, rateLimit, compress, extra, globalExtra} and enforces the documented byte limits; addExtraParameter/removeExtraParameter/getParameters/getUploadToServer/setUploadToServer are pure data and can reach BEHAVIOR_MATCH; getLastCrashReport returns null and getUploadedReports returns [] (this is Electron-faithful whenever nothing was uploaded, because Electron only returns UPLOADED reports). No minidump, no network: uploading anything requires a future approved spec that (a) names the record source (CrashLedger crash-class facts: pid, exit status, bounded stderr tail, generation) — not a minidump — (b) requires a `net.connect` grant whose URL scope covers submitURL, and (c) treats uploadToServer as an opt-in that the manifest, not the app, decides. The effective default (no upload) is a documented ▲ on the scoreboard with a quirks flag, never a silent downgrade (KEL-127). crashReporter in the renderer is ✘ (Keld renderers have no process object; Electron requires preload+contextBridge anyway).

decisions.question: Which process-gone events can Keld deliver honestly, over which primitive, and with what reason fidelity — given Keld's process family (host, guardian, Bun primary, named roles, engine helpers) differs from Chromium's?
decisions.proposed_answer: Three distinct event sources, one host-emitted event family over the app link, consumed by two Electron facades: (1) webContents/app 'render-process-gone' ← engine web-content-process termination, wired in keld-wv per backend (WKWebView WKNavigationDelegate webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate; WebView2 ICoreWebView2 ProcessFailed with ICoreWebView2ProcessFailedEventArgs2 Reason/ExitCode; WebKitGTK WebKitWebView::web-process-terminated with WebKitWebProcessTerminationReason). Reason fidelity is platform-bound: WebKitGTK → {crashed, oom, killed}; WebView2 → full reason + exitCode (259 STILL_ACTIVE when unresponsive); WKWebView → no reason at all. Proposed ▲: on macOS emit reason 'crashed' with exitCode undefined under a quirks flag `renderProcessGoneReasonCoarse`, because the corpus only stringifies details.reason (draw.io) — never fabricate an exitCode. (2) app 'child-process-gone' (type 'Utility') ← KEL-75 named-role generation exit observed by the supervisor (clean-exit/abnormal-exit/killed by exit status/signal; 'oom' only where the OS says so). (3) The Bun PRIMARY dying has NO Electron analog (Electron's main cannot observe its own death); do not map it to any Electron event. It is a Keld-native contract (KEL-143): the successor generation may read the predecessor's CrashLedger facts through @keld/api, and the renderer sees nothing unless the app chooses to tell it. Events are emitted once per termination, after the engine/supervisor observed it and before any reload Keld performs; window identity survives (host owns it).

decisions.question: What census and counters does app.getAppMetrics() report in Keld, and how does it avoid becoming a second, conflicting process census beside architecture 01 §5.1?
decisions.proposed_answer: getAppMetrics is a cold host CALL that returns one ProcessMetric row per keld-owned process exactly as §5.1 defines the census: host (type 'Browser'), macOS guardian re-exec (type 'Unknown', serviceName 'keld.guardian' — no Electron analog), Bun primary (type 'Utility', serviceName 'keld.primary' — the Electron 'Browser' row is the host because the host owns windows; documented ▲ since Electron apps read the Browser row as 'my main process'), named roles (type 'Utility', serviceName = role name). Engine helper rows are appended only where a public API enumerates them: WebView2 ICoreWebView2Environment8::GetProcessInfos (pid + COREWEBVIEW2_PROCESS_KIND → 'Tab'/'GPU'/'Utility'/'Sandbox helper', memory read by the host via OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) + GetProcessMemoryInfo); absent on macOS (no public WKWebView web-process pid; WebKit XPCs are not the app's children) and on WebKitGTK unless a public pid API is found — documented ▲ 'engine rows omitted'. MemoryInfo uses the same counters §5.1 already names: workingSetSize = resident set (ps RSS / working set), privateBytes = private footprint (Windows per Electron; Keld MAY also fill it elsewhere as a ▲), peakWorkingSetSize where the OS reports it; unit KiB (Electron 'Kilobytes'; divisor to be confirmed, see unknowns). CPUUsage per Electron: first call 0, each call resets the interval for every row at once, interval tracked per API (getAppMetrics vs process.getCPUUsage separately). No row of this API is ever a budget score; §5.1 keeps MEM-IDLE on the harness.
evidence: [fact] Electron: getAppMetrics returns ProcessMetric[] for 'all processes associated with the app'; 'each call starts a new measurement interval for every process at once' (app.md v44.4.5, retrieved 2026-10-06); ProcessMetric fields pid, type (Browser|Tab|Utility|Zygote|Sandbox helper|GPU|Pepper Plugin|Pepper Plugin Broker|Unknown), serviceName, name, cpu, creationTime, memory, sandboxed[mac,win], integrityLevel[win] (structures/process-metric.md)

decisions.question: Can process.getHeapStatistics / getProcessMemoryInfo / getCPUUsage / crash() / hang() be served from Bun alone, and what diverges?
decisions.proposed_answer: Yes for the Bun main role, as a pure facade with no host call: getHeapStatistics ← node:v8.getHeapStatistics() renamed to camelCase and divided to KB (fields totalHeapSize, totalHeapSizeExecutable, totalPhysicalSize, totalAvailableSize, usedHeapSize, heapSizeLimit, mallocedMemory, peakMallocedMemory, doesZapGarbage — all present in Bun 1.4.2's v8 shim); getCPUUsage ← process.cpuUsage() deltas with facade-tracked interval (first call 0, cumulativeCPUUsage seconds since start, idleWakeupsPerSecond = 0 as a ▲ — Electron itself returns 0 on Windows); getProcessMemoryInfo ← Promise of {private, shared, residentSet} where only residentSet (process.memoryUsage().rss/1024) is derivable in Bun; `private`/`shared` need the host (task_info / PROCESS_MEMORY_COUNTERS_EX / smaps_rollup) → ▲ until a host diagnostics call exists; on macOS Electron omits residentSet entirely, so Keld must choose follow-Electron (omit) or extend (quirks flag). process.crash() ← process.abort() (SIGABRT → CrashLedger crash-class record, KELD-RUNTIME-012, restart/backoff — Electron's main-process crash kills the whole app instead: ▲). process.hang() ← busy loop; Keld has no Bun hang watchdog, so nothing observes it (▲/unknown). Renderer-side process.* is ✘ (no Node in Keld renderers; Electron's sandboxed renderer does expose these). getBlinkMemoryInfo/getSystemMemoryInfo: ✘ Blink; system memory via host only.

Scoreboard mark ✘ with 'documented-never' and the briefing's never-list #10 (full CDP / Chromium flags in production webviews) as rationale.
